blocks.x: Where most programs improvise, enterprise ai strategy & roadmapping as we deliver it is sequenced: Align AI to P&L lines and risk mandates — a sequenced portfolio, not a pile of pilots. The sequence matters more than the stack — both are documented here.
What we deliver under this name

Most AI strategies fail at portfolio level: hundreds of use-case ideas, no value discipline, no owner for the controls. We run a six-week Value Mapping Sprint that scores candidate use cases on value density, data readiness, regulatory exposure and operational absorption, then sequences a 24-month roadmap with funding gates tied to measured outcomes rather than delivery milestones.

The output is an operating blueprint: named executive owner per use case, named control owner per model, an architecture baseline, a build-buy-partner decision per layer, and a value case per initiative stated in the CFO's units — contribution margin, loss rate, working capital, or headcount redeployment.

Programs of Enterprise AI Strategy & Roadmapping run in Banking & Financial Services, Insurance & Risk, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Manufacturing & Industrial — always against one named number, always with the baseline signed first.

items: Weeks 1–2 — baseline
Enterprise AI Strategy & Roadmapping starts with the measurement: the metric, the owner, the current number, signed.
Weeks 3–8 — bounded build

Weeks nine through thirteen in Enterprise AI Strategy & Roadmapping are the gate: the working slice is measured against the signed baseline, and the scale decision is written down with the evidence attached.
